findings.section: Design, item 7; Freshness, compatibility and limitations
findings.note: Feature 041 is itself on the human-confirmed selective route, but its implementation may encounter the existing missing-runtime-proof stop. The proposed acceptance command does not exist until this feature is implemented, while FR-001 says plan/spec approval is not acceptance. No bootstrap path is defined; implementation is therefore either blocked or depends on an implicit exception contrary to FR-001.

The contract relies on a human-shaped actor value and `--confirm-ordinary-work`, but defines no way to establish that the caller is a human or that `--actor human:<operator>` is trustworthy. Extending the command-detection guard does not authenticate the CLI caller. An agent or other process able to invoke the operation could record a human-labeled acceptance, undermining FR-001 and audit attribution.

findings.section: Design, items 2 and 7; Freshness, compatibility and limitations
findings.note: Host and session are CLI-supplied labels, but no source or validation mechanism for current host/session metadata is specified. Equality against caller-provided values cannot establish that the acceptance matches the actual current context, so the promised context-change invalidation is unverified. Keep this explicitly operator-attested and stop when current context cannot be established; do not imply the labels validate it.

The event stores a scope digest and rationale, but not the disclosed missing evidence, actual observations, or residual-risk snapshot required by FR-002 and the Assurance acceptance entity. A later audit may be unable to determine what limitation and risk the human accepted.
